findings.explanation: The module call sets `key = google_kms_crypto_key.cloudsource.name`, which resolves to the bare key name (e.g. "example-key"), but `var.key` flows straight into `google_pubsub_topic.pike.kms_key_name` (google_pubsub_topic.tf:3), which requires the fully-qualified resource path `projects/{project}/locations/{location}/keyRings/{keyRing}/cryptoKeys/{name}`. A rules engine can't catch this because both `.name` and `.id` are valid, non-null string attributes on `google_kms_crypto_key` — the policy DSL has no notion of 'this string must be the other attribute'. At apply time this will either fail GCP API validation or silently misconfigure CMEK, depending on provider version, leaving the topic without the intended customer-managed encryption guarantee shown in the example.
findings.remediation: Change `key = google_kms_crypto_key.cloudsource.name` to `key = google_kms_crypto_key.cloudsource.id` in example/examplea/module.cloudsource.tf:5.
findings.title: CMEK reference passes KMS key short name instead of full resource ID to the module's `key` variable

suggested_policies.rationale: google_sourcerepo_repository_iam_member/_binding have zero policy coverage today (coverage_by_type returns none), yet this module's own google_sourcerepo_repository_iam_member.binding (google_sourcerepo_repository_iam_member.tf) grants roles straight from an unvalidated `var.iam_bindings` map of role -> member strings, with no guard against a caller passing allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers as a member. This is the exact same risk shape already covered for Pub/Sub topics (HLD_GCP_153) and subscriptions (HLD_GCP_161) — Cloud Source Repositories deserves the same deterministic check, and the condition (member string must not be allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers) is unambiguous and broadly applicable to any Terraform using these resource types.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_002
name: Cloud Source Repository IAM bindings must not grant access to allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers
principle: network-security
severity: CRITICAL
rationale: |
  Granting allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers on a Cloud Source Repository IAM
  binding allows anyone on the internet to read or write source code in the
  repository, including any secrets or credentials committed to history. The
  repository should only be accessible to specific service accounts or groups.
remediation: |
  Remove the allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers member from the repository IAM
  binding.
resources:
  google_sourcerepo_repository_iam_member:
    path: member
    not_one_of:
      - allUsers
      - allAuthenticatedUsers
  google_sourcerepo_repository_iam_binding:
    all:
      - path: members
        not_contains: allUsers
      - path: members
        not_contains: allAuthenticatedUsers
